scope: Qwen3-8B HBM accelerator, one decode token at position 8,191 with 8,192 positions of KV (prompt token 24 -> 18), composed from exact single-stage RTL jobs (one per layer type + head)
vehicle: HA8 vehicle of main e547a0986 (W12 exact datapath + weight/KV prefetch stream on the r14 streaming controller, 4 stacks/die, CK/2 1.024 ns, REFpb), sources of main e2fb7f4ae (sha256 in each token_result.json)
golden: tools/qwen_hbmacc_position_oracle_gpu.py on the local GPU, 36 layers + head prefilled to P8191 (TP2 29,076 s, TP4 23,623 s); TP2 next 18 / 42297c63, TP4 next 18 / 42282b99; TP2 L0-L2 X and kv_pre identical between the 3-layer and 36-layer runs
exactness: every stage X bit-exact on every die; head token 18 and logit bits = GPU oracle at both design points
lever: --winw (prefetch window, stream words; default 160 unchanged). At 8K the KV segment (86 words TP2) holds window room through attention; w160 blocks the stream (room_block) for TP2. Adopted 224 words (21 MiB, inside the SRAM budget: the runner subtracts it from resident code words).

first_access_exposure.token_start: L0 is SRAM-resident; its 86 (TP2) / 43 (TP4) KV words land during the preroll: kv_wait 4 / 2 cycles
first_access_exposure.note: kv_wait = engine waiting for the layer's whole KV segment to land after qkv; the controller streams at full rate meanwhile (room_block 0), so it is stream time, not lost bandwidth

verdict: >=90%: YES at P8191 with the 224-word window: typical HBM layer 96.2% (TP2) / 95.0% (TP4) of the 4.0 TB/s die peak; as built (160 words) TP2 falls to 89.9%
not_measured_unvalidated: embedding row fetch at token start (~60 cycles est.)

window data served from the stage images (arrival timed, not carried)
preroll: TP2 L1 and TP4 L5/L6 entered with 5,000 ctl cycles of prefetch (HA8 convention); TP4 L20 preroll 1,000 ctl vs its measured tail 1,139 ctl (composed value conservative)
